import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Set a clean style for the plot
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create the scatter plot
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='megapixels',
    y='price_usd',
    hue='sensor_type',
    palette='viridis', # Use a distinct color palette for sensor types
    size='weight_grams', # Use weight_grams to vary marker size, adding another dimension
    sizes=(50, 500), # Define the range for marker sizes
    alpha=0.7, # Add transparency to handle potential overplotting
    edgecolor='w', # Add white edge for better separation of points
    linewidth=0.5
)

# Apply log scale to the y-axis (price) for better distribution visualization
plt.yscale('log')

# Set plot title and labels
plt.title('Camera Price vs. Megapixels by Sensor Type and Weight', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold')
plt.xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Price (USD, Log Scale)', fontsize=12)

# Improve legend placement and appearance
plt.legend(title='Sensor Type / Weight (grams)', bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0.)

# Add a grid for readability
plt.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)

# Adjust plot layout to prevent labels/legend from being cut off
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Set a clean style for the plot
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create the scatter plot
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='megapixels',
    y='price_usd',
    hue='sensor_type',
    palette='viridis', # Use a distinct color palette for sensor types
    size='weight_grams', # Use weight_grams to vary marker size, adding another dimension
    sizes=(50, 500), # Define the range for marker sizes
    alpha=0.7, # Add transparency to handle potential overplotting
    edgecolor='w', # Add white edge for better separation of points
    linewidth=0.5
)

# Apply log scale to the y-axis (price) for better distribution visualization
plt.yscale('log')

# Set plot title and labels
plt.title('Camera Price vs. Megapixels by Sensor Type and Weight', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold')
plt.xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Price (USD, Log Scale)', fontsize=12)

# Improve legend placement and appearance
plt.legend(title='Sensor Type / Weight (grams)', bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0.)

# Add a grid for readability
plt.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)

# Adjust plot layout to prevent labels/legend from being cut off
plt.tight_layout()
